tasks.prompt: Summarise how to restore and verify an etcd snapshot on a cluster that kubeadm manages, including what must happen around the restore.

rubric.text: Stop all API server instances, restore state in all etcd instances, then restart all API servers; do not restore while API servers run
Restore with etcdutl (snapshot restore with --data-dir); restoring with etcdctl is deprecated
For a new data directory, update the etcd manifest's hostPath and also set etcd.local.dataDir in the kubeadm-config ConfigMap, or the next kubeadm upgrade writes a manifest for the old directory
Verify snapshots with etcdutl snapshot status, not the deprecated etcdctl snapshot status

tasks.notes: cross-section: restoring section, etcdutl verification section and the kubeadm-config reconfiguration it points to.

tasks.prompt: Explain which configuration changes made after cluster creation survive a `kubeadm upgrade` and what an operator must do to keep them.

rubric.text: kubeadm upgrade does not reconfigure an existing cluster; reconfiguration is a separate manual procedure
/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml is overwritten on upgrade from the cluster-wide kubelet-config ConfigMap
Whether node-specific kubelet settings will be kept is undecided; until then keep them in kubeadm-flags.env or reapply them to config.yaml after every upgrade
CoreDNS Deployment/Service edits are lost on kubeadm upgrade apply and must be reapplied
kube-proxy runs as a DaemonSet, so node-specific kube-proxy configuration is unsupported
